findings.finding: Semtech raised its Q3 FY27 outlook on 2026-10-15 by 8-K item 7.01, at its Analyst Day and about 10 days before the quarter ended (~Oct 25). Net sales went from $410M +/- $5M to $417.5M +/- $2.5M, adjusted EPS from $1.05 to $1.14 +/- $0.02, and adjusted op margin from 31% to 33% +/- 10 bps. Street consensus ($416.0M / $1.13 per Earnings Whispers) sits at or just below the new midpoint. The reported quarter is therefore close to pre-announced, and any beat is likely about 0.5-1.5% of revenue. In Q2 the company beat its own midpoint by 4% ($341.9M against $328M), but the narrowed range now leaves less room.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell about 10% on 2026-10-15, the day it raised this same quarter's guide, and kept falling. On 2026-08-25, a beat on Q2 with a guide well above consensus bought +10.41%. On 2026-05-26, a beat bought -4.41%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: the number is public and inside a narrowed company range. Consensus near the midpoint, not at the top, is what you would see if the market expects no more than a small upside. Sized near zero.
findings.independence: Consensus figures from Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 2026-11-15 (https://finviz.com/news/422864/semtechs-data-center-surge-faces-a-bar-set-above-its-own-raised-guidance). The same 8-K also underlies the second finding, which is about forward targets, not this quarter.

findings.finding: On the Aug 25 call management said the rest of FY27 is fully booked and more than 70% of FY28 is booked. At the Oct 15 Analyst Day it said data center revenue should more than double in each of FY27 and FY28 (FY30 targets: $3.2B revenue, $2.1B data center, 70% GM, EPS $12.40-13.00). Data center was $100M in Q2 and guided +45% q/q in Q3, about $145M. A Q4 guide consistent with doubling FY27 data center revenue implies further sequential data center growth. The stock is down ~45% from its October peak despite this.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide-driven prints were +10.41% (Aug 2026, guide above consensus), +21.06% (Mar 2025) and +15.14% (Aug 2025). The Analyst Day multi-year targets on Oct 15 got about -10% that day and about -27% within a week.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock trades near $103, against $187 on Oct 9 and 75x trailing EPS at the October level. The sell-off was attributed to doubts about sustaining AI capex and to the long-term targets underwhelming, not to any cut in near-term numbers. If the booked-backlog statement were fully believed, the stock would not sit 47% below its high with puts bid. But the market has heard these statements and chosen to discount them, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: Booked-backlog statement from the Q2 call summary (https://quartr.com/events/semtech-corporation-smtc-q2-2027_3PPTtePD). Targets also in https://business-news-today.com/semtech-targets-3-2bn-revenue-by-2030-as-ai-networking-ambitions-collide-with-stock-sell-off/. All are company statements, so they are not independent of each other.

findings.finding: The cellular module business is held for sale. It produced $48.1M of Q2 net sales at a 22.7% adjusted gross margin, and FY26 cellular revenue was $166M. It is being sold to Compal for $62M, closing expected in Q4 FY27, EPS-neutral per management. A Q4 headline revenue guide that excludes all or part of the quarter's ~$40-48M of cellular sales could print flat to down from Q3's ~$418M. If any estimates still carry cellular, the headline guide would look below consensus on the first read, even though the business left is growing and higher-margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Semtech print carried a divestiture-driven headline step-down. The Analyst Day had already rebased FY26 excluding $166M of cellular.
findings.why_not_priced: Sophisticated models were rebased at the Analyst Day, so most of this is priced. What may not be priced is the first headline read of an after-hours print. I could not verify whether the Q4 consensus is ex-cellular, because search was refused. If it were fully priced, preview pieces would quote an ex-cellular Q4 bar; the one preview found gives no Q4 consensus at all.
findings.independence: Divestiture terms and timing in the Aug 13 8-K and press release (https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260812218014/en/Semtech-Corporation-Announces-Definitive-Agreement-on-Sale-of-Cellular-Module-Business-to-Compal-Electronics). No closing announcement was found as of 2026-11-23.

findings.finding: Nvidia reported Q3 FY27 on 2026-11-17, after Semtech last spoke: revenue $115.8B (+103% y/y) against a $108B guide, data center $107.6B, networking over $21B, and a Q4 guide of $130B +/- 3%. The call cited production scale-out of co-packaged-optics switches. This is a demand read for the optical and copper interconnect that Semtech's data center line (about 35% of Q3 revenue) sells into. The CPO scale-out is also a longer-run substitution risk for pluggable-module component content.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No Semtech-specific history on this line. The stock fell through October and November while hyperscaler and Nvidia numbers rose, so the transmission has recently been weak.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it was a widely read print six days ago, and SMTC closed $109 on Nov 18 and $103.41 today, lower after it. It is filed as a counterparty read for the Q4 guide, not as unpriced information.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a Semtech number. Networking and CPO detail from https://www.sdxcentral.com/news/colette-kress-keeps-nvidia-rolling-in-the-deep-networking-waters-without-jensen/.

findings.finding: Coherent reported fiscal Q1 2027 on 2026-11-04, after Semtech last spoke: revenue ~$2.37B (+50% y/y), datacenter +17% q/q and +85% y/y, 1.6T transceivers ramping rapidly with multiple customers, and a Q2 guide of $2.55-2.75B. Transceiver makers like Coherent are customers for Semtech's 1.6T fiber-edge TIA and driver content, which management said is ramping earlier than modeled.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No Semtech-specific history on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: it is a public print three weeks old. Its relevance is that it confirms the 1.6T ramp Semtech's Q4 guide depends on. If the market had taken it as confirmation for SMTC, the stock would not have fallen from ~$115 to ~$103 since.
findings.independence: Proxy, from a different company than the Nvidia finding. Semtech's own '1.6T ramping earlier than modeled' statement is in the Finviz preview (https://finviz.com/news/422864/semtechs-data-center-surge-faces-a-bar-set-above-its-own-raised-guidance).

findings.finding: MACOM, the closest US-listed peer in data center optical analog (TIAs and drivers), reported on 2026-11-05: record data center revenue of $188.1M (+37% q/q), book-to-bill 1.4, record backlog, FY27 data center growth base case ~80%, and a beat-and-raise guide ($450-460M). Its stock had fallen ~41% from its Oct 6 peak ($353.54) to $209.51 the day before the print, the same drawdown shape as SMTC. The page then shows a later snapshot of $233.13 (+11%). The market also weighed MACOM's capex rising to $100-110M and its book-to-bill falling from 1.6.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is a peer reaction analog, not SMTC history. The page header shows MTSI +17.00% while its feed shows -18.35%, and no clean next-session number was sourced, so the analog is uncertain.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an analog: a peer that de-rated ~40% into a print with raised numbers recovered on a beat-and-raise. If SMTC holders expected the same, the put skew would not sit at +16.7 vol points. Sized small because the peer's reaction number is not cleanly sourced.
findings.independence: MACOM results in its own 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001493594/000149359426000041/ex99_1earningsreleaseq4fy26.htm). The reaction figure is from one page with conflicting numbers.

findings.finding: SMTC goes into the print down 24.4% over 20 sessions and 47.6% off its 52-week high, after a 10% drop on its own Q3 raise (Oct 15), an 8.6% drop on a Northland downgrade (Oct 12), and sector sell-offs on Oct 22 (-8 to -12%) and Oct 30 (-9.4%, after Intel's guidance). None of these was a cut to the company's numbers. Short interest is modest, 6.2-6.8M shares and 1.7-2.6 days as of 30 Sep/1 Oct.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline's seven prior reactions are 4 up and 3 down, median |10.4%|. The Aug 2026 print came after a run-in and bought +10.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is visible to everyone. The positive skew (+16.7) shows the market still pays for further downside, which argues the de-rating is not seen as complete. It is filed small because a sign against a large skew needs a reason the market is wrong, and the only reason here is that the sell-off was macro and sector-led rather than company-led. Short interest is too low to supply a squeeze.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call management said secured capacity may be insufficient for FY28 demand, especially in the second half. Semtech bought HieFo, an InP laser and gain-chip maker, for $34M in March 2026 and began an investment and hiring plan at its Alhambra site. The Q3 print could carry a capex step-up or wafer prepayments. That spending would fund capacity for demand management says is already over 70% booked for FY28.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No Semtech history on this line. MACOM's capex rise to $100-110M was cited as a concern around its Nov 5 print.
findings.why_not_priced: The capacity statement is public (Aug 25 call). What is not public is the size of any capex or prepayment step-up. Spending against booked demand is a zero or a positive, so this is sized at 0. It is filed so the panel sees the capex question.
findings.independence: Capacity statement in the Q2 call summary (https://quartr.com/events/semtech-corporation-smtc-q2-2027_3PPTtePD).

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly positive: strong counterparty prints after the company last spoke, a pre-raised quarter, and a peer that recovered after the same de-rating. That cuts against the +16.7 put skew and the -24% run-in, so p_up is held at 53 rather than 55-58. A crowded short is ruled out by short interest at about 2 days to cover.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): the Oct 15 guidance raise was sold about 10%, so the forward-guide finding went from +1.5 to +1.0.
Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the Q3 print sits inside a narrowed company range set ~10 days before quarter end, so the reported-quarter finding went from +0.3 to +0.2.
Lesson 5 (proxy smaller): MACOM's peer-reaction analog rests on a page with conflicting numbers, so it went from +0.8 to +0.5. The Coherent read went from +0.5 to +0.4.

Lesson 7 (sign against strong skew): the positioning finding went from +0.5 to +0.3. Short interest is about 2 days to cover, so there is no squeeze mechanism to justify a larger long. p_up went from 55 to 53.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): capex/capacity spend funds demand management describes as fully booked for FY27 and over 70% booked for FY28, so it went from -0.3 to 0.0.
